If you intentionally run shared-user access, set agents.defaults.sandbox.mode="all", keep tools.fs.workspaceOnly=true, deny runtime/fs/web tools unless required, and keep personal/private identities + credentials off that runtime.
findings.evidence:
Heuristic signals indicate this gateway may be reachable by multiple users:
- channels.telegram.groupPolicy="allowlist" with configured group targets
Runtime/process tools are exposed without full sandboxing in at least one context.
Potential high-impact tool exposure contexts:
- agents.defaults (sandbox=off; runtime=[exec, process]; fs=[read, write, edit, apply_patch]; fs.workspaceOnly=false)
- agents.entries.main (sandbox=off; runtime=[exec, process]; fs=[read, write, edit, apply_patch]; fs.workspaceOnly=false)
OpenClaw's default security model is personal-assistant (one trusted operator boundary), not hostile multi-tenant isolation on one shared gateway. For multiple users or organizations, run one isolated Gateway cell per tenant: https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/multi-tenant-hosting

workspace_governance_truth_check returned critical.
findings.remediation: Inspect the attached findings before trusting the workspace posture.

evidence.issue: TOOLS.md does not clearly preserve approval gating for sensitive edits outside the workspace
evidence.recommendation: Restore explicit approval-gated wording for config/credential/startup/service/plugin/runtime edits outside the workspace path.

evidence.issue: Queue active-workflow section does not identify WF40 as the active workflow
evidence.recommendation: Reconcile OpenClaw Parallel Pilot Queue before using it as the live control surface, or document the WF40 residual-proof exception while another workflow is active.

evidence.issue: Queue next approved item does not match the WF40 cron-proof / repeated-stability residue recorded in the registry
evidence.recommendation: Reconcile the queue next-approved item and registry next-pass text before spawning the next lane, or document the WF40 residual-proof exception while another workflow is active.

evidence.issue: Queue paused-follow-up section does not preserve WF37 review-only/delivery/fail-closed scheduler posture
evidence.recommendation: Restore WF37 as paused follow-up, not active or scheduler-promoted.

evidence.issue: Queue does not clearly preserve WF39 as closed with handoff back to WF38
evidence.recommendation: Restore WF39 closeout/handoff text or update both queue and registry if the workflow was intentionally reopened.

evidence.issue: Workspace Structure Protocol no longer clearly documents the approved root exceptions
evidence.recommendation: Keep root exceptions explicit so root-drift validators do not become folklore.

evidence.issue: Workspace Structure Protocol no longer states that a root 00/ layer is disallowed
evidence.recommendation: Restore the no-root-00 rule or document the approved structural change.

evidence.issue: TOOLS.md does not make the DB lifecycle manifest discoverable enough for weekly hygiene
evidence.recommendation: Add a DB lifecycle route that points at db_lifecycle_manifest.py --write --validate and preserves owner approval before archive/delete.

evidence.issue: DB lifecycle manifest has archive-ready candidates awaiting owner decision
evidence.recommendation: Review the manifest and use db_lifecycle_archive_apply.py only after explicit owner approval.

evidence.issue: finance-stack-snapshot.sqlite is not represented in the DB lifecycle manifest
evidence.recommendation: Regenerate the manifest or update lifecycle rules if the snapshot was intentionally archived.

evidence.issue: TOOLS.md no longer states the current channel hardening posture clearly enough to verify
evidence.recommendation: Keep the no-channel posture or the approved Telegram exception explicit before trusting channel expansion.

evidence.issue: An enabled chat channel appears in config without a matching approved exception
evidence.recommendation: Disable the channel again or update TOOLS.md only after intentional operator approval.

evidence.issue: Telegram plugin appears enabled without a matching approved exception
evidence.recommendation: Disable Telegram plugin again or update TOOLS.md only after intentional operator approval.

evidence.issue: Telegram owner allow entries appear without a matching approved exception
evidence.recommendation: Remove stale Telegram owner authority or document the approved policy change.
